stem.text: Classify the series \( \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{5 \left(-1\right)^{n + 1}}{\sqrt[3]{n + 3}} \) as absolutely convergent, conditionally convergent, or divergent.

answer_key.label: The series converges conditionally, because it passes the alternating series test while the series of absolute values diverges.

worked_solution.text: Test the series of absolute values, \( \sum \frac{5}{\sqrt[3]{n + 3}} \). By limit comparison with \( \sum \frac{1}{n^{\frac{1}{3}}} \), the ratio of terms tends to \( 5 \), so both series behave alike.
That p-series has p = \( \frac{1}{3} \), not more than 1, so the series of absolute values diverges.
The given series alternates, its terms decrease, and they approach 0, so it converges by the alternating series test. It converges conditionally.

options.label: The series converges conditionally, because it passes the alternating series test while the series of absolute values diverges.
The series converges absolutely, because it passes the alternating series test while the series of absolute values diverges.
options.derivation: the absolute and conditional labels exchanged

options.label: The series diverges, because the series of absolute values diverges by comparison with a p-series.
options.derivation: the divergence of the absolute series reported as the verdict on the given series

options.label: The series converges absolutely, because it passes the alternating series test, its terms decreasing in size to 0.
options.derivation: absolute values omitted: the alternating series test result reported as absolute convergence
